$comment: Supported Foundry-Edge pairing, metadata version 2. qualification records hosted pairing acceptance separately from actual Foundry publication and verified Edge distribution. Immutable v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.5.4 and v0.5.5 release records are under docs/release-notes/. CI reads edge.image; docs/compatibility.md records the unchanged support envelope.

edge.build: published release v0.9.15; verified distribution at 25b37395ff61bfea0f3ffd189d9011c4984fa755. Foundry v0.5.5 was qualified and published with this pairing

requirements: It retains ferrum-edge#5661 conditional writes, ferrum-edge#4611 proxy association, and namespace-qualified resource identity (ferrum-edge 5db1d77a8, aligned in #409). The qualification checks these contracts against the published release.

GET /proxies/{id}/mcp/tools remains a viewer-readable, namespace-scoped MCP catalog read; viewer-key namespace ceilings apply to every namespace route and deny global routes outside the documented allowlist. Capability parity includes the new read route.

Operator reads of upstreams mask the Consul ACL token, and operator reads of plugin configs mask secrets and credential-bearing endpoint URL components, with redaction placeholders. A POST or PUT of an upstream or plugin config that echoes a placeholder at a masked field is refused with 400 before update merging (ferrum-edge#5925), so for upstreams and plugin configs a placeholder is not a round-trip marker; admin-only consumer credential entries still round-trip [REDACTED]. Admin reads are raw and never refused. Foundry's editors block such a save, for a non-admin role and only at the sites Edge masks, until each field is re-entered or cleared.

Ferrum Edge v0.9.15 is a security release that fixes 26 published Ferrum Edge advisories (5 high, 19 medium, 2 low), including namespace isolation for Gateway API routes, DestinationRule TLS material and Admin API backend TLS references (ferrum-edge#6092/#6094), refusal of native gRPC and WebSocket requests a route's authentication or admission plugins cannot run on (ferrum-edge#6087/#6090), FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME> confinement of plugin-config environment references (ferrum-edge#6086/#6089), a separate gateway-owned X-Authenticated-Identity header for external identities with LDAP consumer_mapping removed (ferrum-edge#6082/#6088), IPv6 prefix grouping and per-principal MCP session caps (ferrum-edge#6079), and separate ferrum-mesh chart workload ServiceAccounts (ferrum-edge#6096/#6084). It retains v0.9.11's MCP charset and JSON-RPC batch inspection fixes (ferrum-edge#5954) and v0.9.13's HTTP/3 retained-request admission (ferrum-edge#6009). Its publication is not a claim that all upstream security issues are fixed.

v0.9.15 changes plugin-config admission that Foundry's templates and guided editor reflect. Every plugin-config environment reference must name FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME> or is refused with 400, so the ai_semantic_firewall, ai_stream_router, api_chargeback_sink and proxy_alerts templates reference FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_* names, and the plugin-defaults contract expects the two unset-variable refusals Edge now returns for ai_stream_router and proxy_alerts. LdapAuthConfig drops consumer_mapping (refused with 400; no Foundry template or form sets it). RateLimitingConfig adds ipv6_prefix (1-128, default 64), which the guided rate-limiting editor models; McpGatewayConfig adds sessions.max_sessions_per_principal and BodyValidatorConfig grpc_max_decompressed_size_bytes now has minimum 1, both left to the raw JSON editor and Edge admission. X-Authenticated-Identity is gateway-owned and refused as a configured header destination at config load; Foundry neither displays nor sets it and shows Edge's 400 as returned. Where the admin ns claim is enforced, as in this qualification (FERRUM_ADMIN_REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_CLAIM=true), an operator may set backend_tls_client_cert_path, backend_tls_client_key_path and backend_tls_server_ca_cert_path only to inline PEM, system:// or a k8s:// Secret in the addressed namespace; the proxy and upstream forms state the rule and show Edge's 400 rather than refusing locally. Data-plane 403s for gRPC and WebSocket protocol flavors, Connection-nomination handling, HTTP/3 and mesh changes are data-plane behavior with no admin contract change for Foundry; Foundry references no Helm chart.

Foundry v0.5.5 retains guarded-write policy #542, first shipped in v0.5.2 (#544): guarded replacement and deletion refuse an initial fresh verification read without one nonempty quoted visible-ASCII strong ETag, before any PUT/DELETE. Explicit unguarded calls, low-level helpers and plugin membership plans keep their semantics, and the post-412 untagged refusal is unchanged. The paired release issues strong item ETags, confirmed by the hosted qualification.

Static guided-schema review at 25b37395ff61bfea0f3ffd189d9011c4984fa755: KeyAuthConfig, RateLimitingRuleConfig, CorsConfig and PrometheusMetricsConfig are byte-identical to 9bd4d5f9caa4ebe8f0ea13e76d8a6e2172eaca7d, so their pinned hashes are unchanged. RateLimitingConfig adds only the ipv6_prefix property; its block SHA-256 moves from f6f4c095e2c9f326ba62d87094fb9e8ac3833bba9503476cf01daca1ebc6e4a1 to fc6778eda49ab4999909b430a6c90a8abf38b43f8ddf0bfa1e894c5208033037, the guided editor adds ipv6_prefix, and PLUGIN_SCHEMA_SPEC.ref moves to 25b37395ff61bfea0f3ffd189d9011c4984fa755 with it. The sensitivity source is byte-identical to 9bd4d5f9 (Git blob 827bf3a7c998c7ea9c995093ab38320facbd072a) and its provenance is now 25b37395ff61bfea0f3ffd189d9011c4984fa755.

The canonical pin adopts published contracts-edge-0.9.15 at 6fb64c5dc2e014204c17609fc717d976f3b4589e, release 407246047, after successful main Validate contracts run 37841329610. The same 18 scoped files and descriptions are byte-exact. All 82 plugin entries, provisioning values, manifest schema and all 12 fixtures are unchanged; the plugin catalog records the v0.9.15 config-schema changes in a provenance note, and the complete invalid-expectations file adds a diagnostic-ref route-protocol-admission negative and a gateway-headers availability negative without Foundry adopting those schemas. Shared manifest/report status remains EXISTING/implemented at Alloy owner 81cbb, with Alloy unpublished.

Foundry v0.5.5 qualified against this published Edge release in hosted run 37846502086, attempt 1; source f947a607f0bbb920d508e88568969bbe69e5ed58 was tested at merge 8126d6b771f90bd76e8a54b48ddfa26441175c27, with every job green: Qualification Source, Quality Gate on Node 22 and 24, Pinned Gateway Contract (including capability parity, writable and read-only), Deployment Starter, Critical Journeys, Container Gate (amd64), and Container Gate (arm64). The release and tag evidence is preserved in docs/release-notes/v0.5.5.compatibility.json.

edge_dependencies.what: strong ETag on resource reads and If-Match on PUT/DELETE of proxies, upstreams, consumers, and plugin configs; a malformed If-Match, or one on a route that does not evaluate it, is 400
edge_dependencies.status: first released in Ferrum Edge v0.9.7; retained in Ferrum Edge v0.9.8, v0.9.9, v0.9.10, v0.9.11, v0.9.12, v0.9.13, v0.9.14, and v0.9.15
edge_dependencies.effect_on_pinned_edge: Foundry's write guard sends If-Match with the ETag of its verification read, so a writer that commits between that read and the write is refused with 412; the gateway contract asserts the 412s and the 400s

edge_dependencies.what: optional proxy_id filter on GET /plugins/config (exact match, paginated over the filtered set, invalid value is 400)
edge_dependencies.status: first released in Ferrum Edge v0.9.7; retained in Ferrum Edge v0.9.8, v0.9.9, v0.9.10, v0.9.11, v0.9.12, v0.9.13, v0.9.14, and v0.9.15
edge_dependencies.effect_on_pinned_edge: a proxy's Plugins tab lists the proxy-scoped configurations targeting it from the filtered collection instead of the whole namespace; a response the filter did not narrow is refused rather than shown
